html:
FILM (Reda et al., Google, ECCV 2022): makes the middle frame between two video frames, also for large motion, from a flow pyramid in both directions and features shared across scales. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: FILM: Frame Interpolation for Large Motion, ECCV 2022, 2022-02-10
  • Original code: https://github.com/dajes/frame-interpolation-pytorch at 33bf477ea2c6
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/dajes/frame-interpolation-pytorch/blob/33bf477ea2c65a2ed1b5f2280ee1f02be06910e8/LICENSE ; https://github.com/dajes/frame-interpolation-pytorch/releases/tag/v1.0.2 ; https://github.com/google-research/frame-interpolation/blob/69f8708f08e62c2edf46a27616a4bfcf083e2076/README.md
  • Training data: Vimeo-90K (septuplets / triplets for frame interpolation) (google-research/frame-interpolation README "Datasets": Vimeo-90K triplets are the training set (film_net-Style.gin).)
  • Options: cuda_graphs = True (speed only)
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: film
  • Outputs: frame
  • Input size: any H x W >= 64, padded to a multiple of 64
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): film 1988x2880 (13.0 GiB peak allocated, 15.3 reserved)
  • film original 1080x1920: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); the TorchScript release as inference.py, dt 0.5, zero pad to 64 (centred), --fp16: model.half()
  • film load / first call: original 0.29 s / 0.946 s, portable 0.19 s / 0.529 s, kernels 0.33 s / 0.445 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 5e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.001 and p99 <= 0.005 (absolute error of the output frame).
